title: A tale of two teeth
hook: Different tooth shapes meet food differently.

knows: Animals have body structures and life histories.
doesNotKnow: Connect a broad tooth surface with grinding.

misconception: A familiar animal feature always has the first explanation that comes to mind.
objective: Connect a broad tooth surface with grinding.

claims.text: Which tooth shape is better suited to crushing and grinding plant material? The stage contrasts a broad ridged chewing surface with a pointed one. Mammal teeth can have different shapes associated with different feeding tasks; a pointed tooth and a grinding tooth do not do the same job.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, animal nutrition and mammalian dentition, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The diagram and its labels are schematic, not to scale and not an observation. Tooth shapes · schematic
A grazing mammal needs to crush food. Which kind of tooth surface is most relevant? Broad ridged chewing surfaces can crush and grind food.
